narrative.overview: D'titans Food should feel like a warm, well-kept kitchen notebook rather than a catering brochure. The system is built from uncoated paper, chocolate ink, caramel thread, printed photographs, and generous pauses between thoughts. Its job is to make home cooking feel considered and personal, not corporate. The page moves in alternating fields: warm ivory for editorial calm, white for the menu index, deep chocolate for catering and the recipe book, and one committed caramel field for the kitchen's principles. Typography carries the hierarchy; photography carries the appetite; rules and small tabular numbers carry the sense of a ledger kept by hand. The composition is deliberately asymmetric, but the reading order stays obvious. Confirmed rejection: no generic SaaS dashboard styling, no equal-card feature grid, no glossy product-platform claims. Placeholder photography, draft menu copy, and unavailable platform links must be visibly identified until the real material replaces them.
keyCharacteristics: Warm Ivory and White paper fields, Chocolate ink, Caramel Gold as the singular thread.
Oversized Cormorant Garamond display paired with quiet DM Sans utility text.
Hairline rules, menu-ledger rows, tabular numerals, and square photo plates.
Photographs treated as printed material rather than floating rounded cards.
One committed caramel field and two deep chocolate fields create a strong, warm rhythm.
Motion is restrained: a single hero reveal, confident hover states, reduced-motion always honored.

rules.name: The One Warm Field Rule
rules.body: Caramel is an event. One full caramel section per page; everywhere else it is a thread, never a background wash.

rules.name: The Legibility First Rule
rules.body: Small text never sits directly in Caramel Gold on Ivory or White. Use Caramel Ink on light grounds and Caramel Soft on chocolate grounds.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Cormorant never handles interface instructions, and DM Sans never carries a display headline. The hierarchy depends on keeping those roles absolute.

rules.name: The Short Thought Rule
rules.body: Display and headline text should break into two or three deliberate lines. Avoid full-width paragraphs set in serif.

rules.name: The Ledger Beat Rule
rules.body: Every section opens with more space above its heading than below it, then introduces a one-pixel rule before dense repeated content. Repeated items align on a shared left edge even when imagery offsets the rhythm.

rules.name: The Printed Plate Rule
rules.body: Images are rectangular prints with square corners and a hairline edge. Do not turn them into floating rounded cards or apply glass effects.

rules.name: The Straight Edge Rule
rules.body: If a new element needs to feel premium, reduce its radius rather than adding one. Paper does not have pills.

dos: Do use Warm Ivory and Paper White for long reading surfaces, with Chocolate Ink as the default text.
Do keep Caramel Gold to one full field, thin rules, and small deliberate accents.
Do set display headings in Cormorant Garamond with italic emphasis on the second thought.
Do use square photographs with hairline edges and soft print-style shadows only where a physical object is implied.
Do preserve the 82rem shell, asymmetric grids, and the 7/5 gallery rhythm.
Do mark synthetic or placeholder photography and keep unavailable actions visibly unavailable.
Do give primary controls at least 44px of touch height and keep visible keyboard focus.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion; the hero reveal is the page's single authored motion moment.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, gradient text, or a second display face.
Don't turn the menu, services, or story into equal rounded cards with shadows.
Don't use DM Sans for display headings or Cormorant for interface labels.
Don't place small Caramel Gold text on Ivory or White; use Caramel Ink or Chocolate.
Don't round photographs, book surfaces, or large fields; 2px is the interactive ceiling.
Don't fill empty space with generic icon tiles, decorative sparklines, or badge rows.
Don't claim a platform integration, live order link, price, package, or lead time that the business has not supplied.
Don't recreate or approximate the D'titans Food logo; use the supplied asset unaltered.
